scores.evidence: Append-only double-entry ledger; integer minor units plus currency; UUIDv7 IDs; immutable, versioned prices and plans
scores.rationale: Claims are accurate (RLS non-bypass role, SAQ A with hosted fields, outbox, serializable writes); minor gaps such as gap-free numbering per tenant vs jurisdiction specifics and no stated rounding stage.

scores.evidence: Build the ledger, rating and invoicing (the differentiator and system of record). Buy payment execution (Stripe or Adyen), tax
scores.rationale: Covers core billing capabilities with explicit deferrals and interpretation of ambiguous 'tenant'; entitlements/access control on non-payment and dunning policy are thin.

scores.evidence: PSP sits behind an interface and holds no source-of-truth state
scores.rationale: Consistent design with clear ownership and consistency split; minor loose ends (entitlements, merchant-of-record question left open affecting structure).

scores.evidence: Property-based tests on ≥ 1M generated sequences (duplicates, out-of-order events, retries, plan changes, rounding); replay from the event log
scores.rationale: Validation is tied to specific risks, early (V0–V2), with checkable criteria labeled as design parameters/assumptions, shadow billing, and production reconciliation/canary.

scores.evidence: UNKNOWN: peak usage events/s and tenant count at 12 months; product owner and sales supply before Phase 3
scores.rationale: Assumptions, unknowns, owners and what changes if wrong are explicit; numbers are labeled and no invented facts.

scores.evidence: 0 double charges and 0 ledger/PSP mismatches; fault injection in PSP test mode (duplicate, reordered, dropped webhooks; timeouts; retries)
scores.rationale: Covers duplicates, reordering, noisy tenants, cross-tenant leaks, charge caps and kill-switch; late usage events, dispute handling and dunning details and named owners of discrepancies are thin.

scores.evidence: Redeploy the prior image and flip the flag. Migrations stay backward-compatible, so rollback never needs a schema revert.
scores.rationale: Deployment, rollback, SLOs, restore drill, on-call, runbooks are concrete and sized for small team; incident ownership is somewhat light.

scores.evidence: Storage cost | No number | UNKNOWN: event volume × retention.
scores.rationale: Build-vs-buy and storage drivers are recognized, but PSP/tax vendor fees, engineering cost and cost controls beyond quotas are barely quantified.

scores.evidence: R3: financial records are legally retained and can't be rewritten
scores.rationale: Decisions are explicitly ranked by reversibility with validation, revisit triggers, PSP seam with export and second-PSP stub, and deferrals.

scores.evidence: Modular monolith plus one worker process, with module boundaries per domain
scores.rationale: Simplest workable architecture with managed services and explicit pull-forward triggers; some ceremony (many V-checks) but justified for money.

scores.evidence: Exit check (V0): The request succeeds with one trace across every tier. A deploy and a rollback succeed through the pipeline.
scores.rationale: Walking skeleton, risk-ordered phases with dependencies, checkable exits and failure actions make it startable immediately.
